name: Kenya
gaps: No independent bird club with its own website or verifiable social page found for Nakuru (a Facebook group exists but could not be confirmed with real content), Kisumu, Mombasa town or Kakamega, despite searching each by name and in combination with Nature Kenya's Site Support Group network.
Nature Kenya's Site Support Groups (about 30 nationwide) are mostly community groups without their own websites beyond Dakatcha Woodland and Friends of Arabuko Sokoke Forest, which are included here.

groups.name: Nature Kenya
groups.blurb: East Africa's oldest environmental society and BirdLife partner, running Wednesday morning birdwalks and bird monitoring.

groups.name: Kenya Bird Map
groups.blurb: Citizen science bird atlas project tracking distribution and status of Kenya's 1065 bird species.

groups.name: Tropical Biology Association
groups.blurb: Conservation training charity based in Nairobi and Cambridge, running African field courses in ecology and biology.

groups.name: Friends of Nairobi National Park
groups.blurb: Membership group supporting Nairobi National Park through outings, monitoring and conservation advocacy.

groups.name: Nairobi Bird Ringing Group
groups.blurb: Weekly public bird ringing sessions at the National Museums of Kenya, running since 1994 with Nature Kenya.

groups.name: Kenya Bird of Prey Trust
groups.blurb: Naivasha based charity researching and protecting Kenya's raptors, with public engagement and rehabilitation work.

groups.name: Kijabe Environment Volunteers
groups.blurb: Community conservation group protecting the Kikuyu Escarpment forest, a Nature Kenya Site Support Group.

groups.name: A Rocha Kenya
groups.blurb: Conservation organisation working in Arabuko Sokoke coastal forest and coastal Kenya habitats.

groups.name: Friends of Arabuko Sokoke Forest
groups.blurb: Community group supporting conservation of Arabuko Sokoke, an Important Bird Area on the Kenyan coast.

groups.name: Dakatcha Woodland Project
groups.blurb: Community led conservation of Dakatcha Woodland near Malindi, habitat of the endangered Clarke's weaver.

name: Tanzania
gaps: Zanzibar Birdwatching Society (ZABISO) is a real, community based group but its domain zabiso.org now serves a parked, ad injected redirect page, so no working link was found for it.

No independent bird club with its own site or verifiable social presence found for Arusha, Dar es Salaam or Zanzibar beyond the countrywide Birding Tanzania Facebook group; Nature Tanzania's own site describes itself as the only bird focused conservation NGO in the country.
Tanzania Bird Atlas's site only resolves over plain http, not https.

groups.name: Wildlife Conservation Society of Tanzania
groups.blurb: Independent conservation organisation founded 1988, BirdLife partner, supporting wildlife conservation across Tanzania.

groups.name: Nature Tanzania
groups.blurb: The BirdLife partner and only bird focused conservation NGO in Tanzania, running research and outreach programmes.

groups.name: Tanzania Bird Atlas
groups.blurb: Citizen science project mapping the distribution of Tanzania's bird species by region.

groups.name: Birding Tanzania
groups.blurb: Public Facebook community for birders across Tanzania sharing sightings, trip reports and identification help.

name: Uganda
gaps: NatureUganda's university branches (Gulu, Islamic University in Uganda, Muni, Busitema, Mbarara, Kabale) each have a named coordinator but no public site or social page of their own, so were left out rather than listed with only a personal email.

Nature Palace Foundation and Uganda Bird Club (UBC) were checked but not included: the former is a general community and climate NGO rather than a birding group, and the latter could only be found through a tour operator's marketing page, not an independent source.

groups.name: NatureUganda
groups.blurb: BirdLife partner promoting understanding and conservation of nature, coordinating birding activities across Uganda.

groups.name: Uganda Women Birders
groups.blurb: Inclusive birding community founded 2013 to increase women's participation in bird guiding and birding.

groups.name: Uganda Bird Guides Club
groups.blurb: One of East Africa's oldest bird guiding networks, running excursions and training for members across Uganda.

groups.name: Uganda Young Birders
groups.blurb: Youth birding club running weekend excursions and mentoring young birdwatchers across Uganda.

groups.name: Avian Conservation Uganda
groups.blurb: Nonprofit running monthly field excursions, a school of ornithology and community bird conservation projects.

groups.name: Entebbe Birding Club
groups.blurb: Community based club bringing bird and nature enthusiasts together for weekly outings around Entebbe.

name: Nigeria
gaps: The Nigerian Bird Atlas Project's own domain nibap.ng has an expired SSL certificate, so its African Bird Atlas Project portal was used instead.
No independent bird club found with own presence for Lagos or Abuja beyond the groups listed here.

groups.name: Nigerian Conservation Foundation
groups.blurb: The national bird society and BirdLife partner, coordinating conservation and education.

groups.name: NCF Bird Club
groups.blurb: Volunteer led birding group running walks, field trips and conservation projects across Nigeria.

groups.name: A.P. Leventis Ornithological Research Institute
groups.blurb: Research and training centre for ornithology and bird conservation at University of Jos.

groups.name: Nigerian Bird Atlas Project
groups.blurb: Citizen science bird atlas run with APLORI, coordinating over 20 bird clubs across Nigeria's states.

groups.name: Jos Bird Club
groups.blurb: Nature enthusiasts birding together every second Saturday of the month around Jos and the Plateau.

groups.name: Ibadan Bird Club
groups.blurb: Local birding community running outings and nature exploration around Ibadan and Oyo State.

groups.name: Calabar Bird Club
groups.blurb: Local birding community running identification training and outings around Calabar and Cross River State.

name: Ghana
gaps: No independent regional bird club found with its own site for Kumasi, Cape Coast or Mole National Park; a Ghana Bird Atlas Project Facebook group turned up but could not be confirmed with real visible content.

groups.name: Ghana Wildlife Society
groups.blurb: The national bird society and BirdLife partner, organizing monthly public birdwalks and conservation work.

groups.name: Wildlife Clubs of Ghana
groups.blurb: The junior wing of Ghana Wildlife Society, running nature and bird clubs in schools nationwide.

groups.name: Ghana Bird Ringing Scheme
groups.blurb: Bird ringing programme based at the University of Ghana, Legon, studying bird populations and movements.

groups.name: A Rocha Ghana
groups.blurb: Conservation organisation working on bird surveys and habitat protection at Keta Lagoon and beyond.

name: Namibia
gaps: Namibia Crane Working Group is referenced across multiple third party sources but has no live dedicated website of its own.
REST (Rare and Endangered Species Trust) has rebranded as Pangolins International and no longer centres on birds, so was left out.
No independent club found for Swakopmund, Erongo or the Walvis Bay wader counts beyond the Namibia Bird Club.
The Southern African Bird Atlas Project (SABAP2) covers this country too, but it is one regional portal rather than a group of its own here, so it is listed once under South Africa.

groups.name: Namibia Bird Club
groups.blurb: Ornithological society founded in 1962, running guided walks and surveys. Publishes journal Lanioturdus and newsletter Bird Call.

groups.name: Vultures Namibia
groups.blurb: Research and monitoring project tracking and protecting Namibia's six vulture species, with public sighting reports.

name: Botswana
gaps: The former Botswana Bird Club merged into BirdLife Botswana decades ago and no longer exists separately.
Kalahari Conservation Society and Okavango area guide associations were checked but are general wildlife or professional guiding bodies, not birding communities.
No independent bird club with its own site found for Maun, Francistown or Gaborone beyond BirdLife Botswana.
The Southern African Bird Atlas Project (SABAP2) covers this country too, but it is one regional portal rather than a group of its own here, so it is listed once under South Africa.

groups.name: BirdLife Botswana
groups.blurb: The national BirdLife partner, formerly the Botswana Bird Club. Runs education, research and community mobilization for bird conservation.

name: Zimbabwe
gaps: BirdLife Zimbabwe's Harare, Bulawayo, Mashonaland and Matabeleland branches are real and run their own outings (documented in the Babbler newsletter) but have no independently linkable website or social page of their own separate from the national office.
The Southern African Bird Atlas Project (SABAP2) covers this country too, but it is one regional portal rather than a group of its own here, so it is listed once under South Africa.

groups.name: BirdLife Zimbabwe
groups.blurb: The national bird society and BirdLife partner, founded 1951. Coordinates branches and citizen science atlassing and bird record submission.

groups.name: Birding Zimbabwe
groups.blurb: Public Facebook community for birders across Zimbabwe, home to over 650 species, sharing sightings and trips.

groups.name: West African Bird Study Association
groups.blurb: Founded 1994 by young Gambians, running bird study clubs and conservation education across the country.

groups.name: Gambia Bird Guides Association
groups.blurb: Association of over 75 licensed Gambian bird guides promoting professional and responsible birdwatching.

name: Senegal
gaps: APALIS and GEPOC, Casamance area ornithological groups mentioned in earlier research, and Oceanium de Dakar still have no independently verified website or social page.

groups.name: Nature Communautés Développement
groups.blurb: The national BirdLife partner, a volunteer led association for nature and bird conservation across Senegal.

groups.name: Atlas des oiseaux du Sénégal
groups.blurb: Citizen science bird atlas run with Cheikh Anta Diop University, mapping Senegal's bird distribution.

name: Cameroon
gaps: Cameroon Biodiversity Conservation Society could only be found on an old, likely dormant personal free.fr page and was left out.
Cameroon currently has no BirdLife International partner. Green Cameroon is a real, active NGO but is a general environmental and youth education group, not bird focused.

groups.name: Cameroon Wildlife Conservation Society
groups.blurb: National professional society of over 160 wildlife managers and researchers conserving Cameroon's biodiversity.

name: Côte d'Ivoire
gaps: Société Ivoirienne d'Ornithologie is newly formed and does not yet appear to have its own standalone website; its public communications run through the Les Oiseaux de Côte d'Ivoire Facebook page used here.

groups.name: Société Ivoirienne d'Ornithologie
groups.blurb: Ivorian ornithological society building a national bird atlas and running local sections and youth outreach.

groups.name: Station Ornithologique du Bénin
groups.blurb: Runs Benin's national bird ringing centre and courses, and coordinates bird research and monitoring.

groups.name: Oiseaux Horizons
groups.blurb: Volunteer association working to safeguard and promote the birds of Benin.

groups.name: Conservation Society of Sierra Leone
groups.blurb: Sierra Leone's oldest environmental NGO and BirdLife partner, running wetland bird surveys and water bird censuses.

groups.name: Society for the Conservation of Nature of Liberia
groups.blurb: The national BirdLife partner, running a Birdwatch Club and community conservation across Liberia.

name: Cape Verde
gaps: Biosfera operates under several related domains for different islands; biosferacaboverde.com and biosfera1.com also appear live but bioscaboverde.com, with its own dedicated birds page, was used here to avoid ambiguity.

groups.name: BIOS.CV
groups.blurb: Conservation NGO monitoring and protecting Cape Verde's seabirds, sea turtles and endemic species.

groups.name: Fundação Príncipe
groups.blurb: Conservation NGO on Príncipe Island protecting its endemic birds and habitats through local community programmes.

name: Gabon
gaps: Confirmed genuinely empty: the African Bird Club states there is currently no BirdLife Partner in Gabon, and no independent ornithological society or bird club with a public presence was found despite searching in French and English.

name: DR Congo
gaps: Confirmed genuinely empty: DR Congo has no BirdLife partner. The only national body found, ICCN, is a government agency managing protected areas with no public membership or volunteer birding programme, so was excluded.

name: Rwanda
gaps: ACNR's own domain acnrwanda.org is no longer live, so its Facebook page is used here instead.

groups.name: Association pour la Conservation de la Nature au Rwanda
groups.blurb: Membership association of around 135 members founded by students and teachers, conserving Rwanda's biodiversity.

name: Mozambique
gaps: AACEM has no independent website found beyond its Facebook group.
The Southern African Bird Atlas Project (SABAP2) covers this country too, but it is one regional portal rather than a group of its own here, so it is listed once under South Africa.

groups.name: AACEM (Birds Mozambique)
groups.blurb: Community of birding enthusiasts and successor to the Mozambique Bird Club, promoting bird conservation and awareness.
